name: espiad
tagline: A Spanish-language library of digital product offers pulled from Meta Ad Library, hand-researched and refreshed daily, with filters and market trend views.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Advertised in Argentine pesos, so any USD figure drifts weekly.

verdictSummary: The software here is a filterable table over a database, which an agent will hand you before lunch. The product is the database: offers spotted in Meta Ad Library, checked by a human, and added every single day. Meta's public Ad Library API only serves political and social issue ads, so there is no clean faucet for the commercial creatives this depends on, and scraping the web UI is a fragile, ToS-hostile hobby. You can absolutely build a personal offer tracker, you just become the person doing the daily research. If the daily research is the thing you were paying to skip, building the shell does not help.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where you log ad offers you find yourself, tag niche, angle, funnel type and landing page, then filter and chart which ones keep running.
requirements: Your own time in Meta Ad Library, manual entry or a logged-in browser session you control
Optional: an OpenAI-compatible API key for auto-tagging pasted ad copy
whatYouLose: The actual corpus: thousands of already-found offers you did not have to hunt
Daily additions by someone whose job is scanning the Ad Library so you do not
Human filtering, most of what is running is junk and someone already threw it out
Trend views that only mean something across a large dataset, your 40 saved ads will not produce a trend
Reliable access to ad creatives and landing pages, which Meta does not hand out through an API
moatNotes: Manual daily curation is an unglamorous moat but a real one: it cannot be cloned by an agent, only out-labored.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is usually trying to find a product to sell this week, not to build a research tool. Paying a monthly fee to skip three hours a day of scrolling Meta Ad Library is a straightforward trade, and the curation is the part they cannot shortcut. A personal clone gives you a nicer spreadsheet and the exact same amount of hunting.
notes: The filters and charts are a weekend; the library is not. The moat is a person opening Meta Ad Library every morning and throwing out the 95 percent that is garbage.
prompt:
Build a local-first "offer tracker" for researching digital product ads. Single user, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/offers.db
- Drizzle for schema and migrations
- Recharts for the two charts

Data model, table `offers`:
- id, title, advertiser, niche, country, language
- offerType (course, ebook, saas, template, community, other)
- angle (free text), funnelType (vsl, quiz, webinar, direct, lead-magnet, other)
- priceText, landingUrl, adLibraryUrl
- adCopy (text), creativeNotes (text)
- firstSeen (date), lastChecked (date), stillRunning (boolean)
- rating 1-5, verdict (watching, testing, dead), notes
- createdAt, updatedAt

Screens:
1. /offers: dense table, sortable columns, filter bar for niche, offerType, funnelType, country, stillRunning, verdict, rating, and a text search across title, advertiser, angle, adCopy. Filters persist in the URL.
2. /offers/new and /offers/[id]: full edit form. Include a "paste ad copy" textarea that, if OPENAI_API_KEY is set in .env, calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint once to suggest niche, offerType, funnelType and angle as prefilled fields the user can overwrite. If the key is absent, hide that button entirely. No other network calls.
3. /dashboard: two charts, offers added per week, and count of stillRunning offers grouped by niche. Plus a "stale" list of offers whose lastChecked is older than 14 days.

Also:
- A "check" action on each row that sets lastChecked to today and toggles stillRunning, one click.
- CSV import and export of the whole table, so the data is never trapped.
- Seed script with 5 fake rows so the UI is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope: scraping Meta, any Ad Library API integration, screenshot capture, auth, multi-user, hosting. Entries are added by hand or imported from CSV.

Write README.md with setup, env vars, and a one-line honest warning that this ships empty and the research is on the user.
